title: The Blaschka Object Network — Customs and Border Regulation Archive Register
scope: Archival targets created when Blaschka shipments crossed fiscal, customs, quarantine and inspection regimes. The register separates German export/customs administration from U.S. customs and agricultural quarantine and uses the 1923 and 1929 Ware Collection shipments as source-rich test cases.
methodological_guard: An administrative fonds is included because its jurisdiction and dates overlap a documented Blaschka regulatory encounter; no individual government file is claimed to concern Blaschka until a name, case mark, consignee, date or transaction is located. Workshop descriptions of officials and rules are preserved as primary evidence even when the corresponding state file has not survived or been identified.

cases.primary_problem: German export permission, export-tax valuation and physical customs revision threatened to require unpacking of fragile models before export. Rudolf reorganised the encounter so that packing could be completed under customs observation and the cases sealed.
documented_actions: claim for exemption or special treatment in export taxation
valuation in the context of postwar currency instability
rail dispatch from Dresden toward Bremen

archive_targets.jurisdiction_note: The Landesfinanzamt/Oberfinanzpräsident Dresden supervised customs and excise through Abteilung II and was the direct superior authority for customs officials in its district after the 1919 Reich finance reorganisation.
archive_targets.research_question: Do files on export duties, customs exemptions, art/scientific teaching objects, Dresden customs offices or extraordinary export permissions contain the 1923 Blaschka case?

archive_targets.jurisdiction_note: After the Reichsfinanzverwaltung reform, the Dresden district included Hauptzollamt Dresden-Altstadt and Dresden-Neustadt and subordinate customs offices responsible for collection and supervision of duties and excise.
archive_targets.guard: The public holdings overview establishes the responsible customs structure but does not expose a Blaschka-specific Dresden customs file.

archive_targets.jurisdiction_note: The ministry's relevant subject fields included customs, commercial treaties, consulates, transport, industrial exhibitions, craft and commercial schools, banking and trade matters.
archive_targets.research_question: Use only if the 1923 dispute escalated beyond routine customs administration into economic-policy, export or consular correspondence.

cases.shipment: incoming Blaschka glass-model boxes to Harvard
cases.primary_problem: A customary Boston customs-broker arrangement had become obsolete because consignee E. A. Snow was no longer in business, forcing Harvard to reassemble the clearance chain. The shipment was then opened at the University Museum under a custom-house inspector.
documented_actions: freight and charges paid from Ware appropriation

archive_target.reference: Record Group 36, Records of the U.S. Customs Service
archive_target.research_question: Search Boston customs records for November 1906 entries, consignee E. A. Snow, Harvard/University Museum, glass models, Rudolf Blaschka, Bremen/North German Lloyd and inspection records.

cases.primary_problem: The cases travelled from New York in bond to Boston and generated a surviving T. D. Downing Co. customs/freight invoice to Harvard.
cases.direct_surviving_document: T. D. Downing Co. invoice dated 20 October 1923, ref. L 16091, for four packages glassware marked RB 1/4.

archive_target.reference: Record Group 36, Records of the U.S. Customs Service
archive_target.research_question: Can Downing ref. L 16091 or RB 1/4 be cross-walked to customs entry, bond, manifest, warehouse, appraisement or clearance paperwork?

cases.shipment: four cases / twenty-seven framed boxes of botanical glass models
cases.primary_problem: Straw or hay used as packing material was reclassified as regulated plant material under U.S. quarantine practice. The border problem therefore attached to the protective packaging rather than the glass objects themselves.
documented_actions: communication between Harvard and Blaschka about acceptable packing material

archive_targets.reference: Record Group 7, Records of the Bureau of Entomology and Plant Quarantine
archive_targets.coverage: 1863–1956; Bureau of Plant Quarantine and predecessors 1912–1952
relevant_series: records of the Bureau of Plant Quarantine and its predecessors
Plant Quarantine Division general correspondence and reports, 1927–1951
archive_targets.research_question: Search 1929 foreign-plant-quarantine correspondence and violation material for packing straw/hay, glass models, Harvard, Boston/New York ports, Germany, or case-specific correspondence.

archive_targets.reference: Record Group 36, Records of the U.S. Customs Service
archive_targets.research_question: Cross-walk any quarantine intervention with the customs entry and port handling of the four cases.

comparative_observation: Customs did not encounter a stable category called 'Blaschka model'. The same shipment could be valued as art/scientific teaching material for export taxation, treated as glassware by a customs broker, moved under bond as freight, inspected physically at a museum, and subjected to plant-quarantine rules because of its straw packing. Regulatory classification therefore changed with jurisdiction and with the material component being examined.
